text.p: Latvia's Staburadze confectionery said on Tuesday that it was optimistic over market prospects in neighbouring Estonia and Lithuania and was also happy with the functioning of the Baltic free trade agreement.

"We manage to sell eight to ten tonnes of produce a month in Estonia, which is a good sign for a country which is in the sphere of influence of Finnish Fazer," Ilmar Rudzitis, Staburadze president, told Reuters.
He also said that Lithuanian producers may see strong competition from Staburadze as it makes its way into their market with the first trial shipments already sold.
"Our quality is no worse and in biscuits we can even offer a better product for a cheaper price," Rudzitis said.
Rudzitis also said that the new Baltic free trade agreement had helped the company.
"We are satisfied with the Baltic free market," referring to both sales oportunities and raw material prices.
He said the company could now buy flour in Latvia at the same prices as in Lithuania.
Staburadze buys flour, sugar, eggs and milk products on the Baltic market and imports all its spices and fragrances.
Staburadze also plans more intensive work on the local Latvian market during 1997 by increasing the number of company shops and by aggresive marketing and pricing.
"The trend of widening the network of Staburadze shops will continue," Rudzitis said.
"We plan to widen the spectrum of our extremely popular, top-ten, cream cakes this year," Rudzitis added.

Rudzitis said that stable quality, advertising and a wide network of own shops was the main way to beat the competition of Hanzas Maiznieks, owned by the Ave Lat group, and Vidzemes Maiznieks and many smaller confectionery firms.
Staburadze also sees an increase in export to Russia and Germany to 10 percent of the planned 7,000 tonnes of produce versus some four percent of last year's 6,300 tonnes.
